captions.detailed: This 3D model is a flat, geometric educational aid demonstrating the Pythagorean theorem using semicircles. It features three flat semicircles positioned along the outer edges of an implied right-angled triangle, leaving the central triangular area hollow. At the right-angle vertex, there is a small curved arc representing the 90-degree angle indicator, along with three tiny cylindrical pins marking the vertices of the triangle.
captions.instruction: Create a parametric OpenSCAD model that visualizes the Pythagorean theorem using semicircles built on the sides of a right triangle. The user should be able to adjust the lengths of leg 'a' and leg 'b', as well as the extrusion height, with the hypotenuse 'c' calculated automatically to position the corresponding semicircles and vertex markers.
captions.factory: The design is constructed using 2D profiles that are extruded to a specified height using 'linear_extrude'. Semicircles for leg 'a' and leg 'b' are created by subtracting a 'square' from a 'circle' and translating them into place. The hypotenuse semicircle is rotated using 'rotate' with an angle calculated via 'asin(b/c)' to align with the hypotenuse. The central triangle module creates the vertex pins using small circles, and the right-angle indicator is made by differencing two concentric circles and subtracting squares to isolate a quadrant.
